before.title: Charge Port Latch Freezes in Cold Weather
before.description: In extreme cold the charge-port door/latch can freeze, preventing the door from opening or the connector from locking/releasing so the car won't start charging or won't release the cable. Early Model 3s (2017-2020, built before the charge-port inlet heater was added in early 2020) are most affected.
before.solution: Use the app's Defrost Car or Controls > Service > Inlet Heater for 10-15 minutes before charging; schedule a departure time so the car preconditions the port. Thaw with warm water in a sealed bag, de-icer, or a hand warmer. If the connector is stuck, use the manual charge-cable release in the trunk. Cars built mid-2020+ have the inlet heater which largely resolves it.
symptoms: Charge port door won't open in cold
Connector won't lock or won't release
Charging won't initiate until port is warmed

before.title: Front Lower Lateral Link / Control Arm Bushing Tears (Clunk)
before.description: Around 40,000-70,000 miles many Model 3/Y owners report a clunk, pop or knock from the front end over bumps, under braking or acceleration. The cause is torn rubber bushings in the front lower lateral link (front lower control arm) and compliance/fore-aft link. When the bushing rubber tears, the arm develops play on its bolt and metal parts contact, producing the clunk. Unlike the squeak, a clunk with steering wander is a safety concern.
before.solution: Tesla sells the arms only as complete assemblies (not the bushings separately), so the standard repair is replacing the affected lateral link / lower control arm assemblies (front lower link OEM PN family 1044351-00-x). Aftermarket press-in bushings or solid bearings (e.g., MountainPass Performance) are available but require a press. Follow with a four-wheel alignment.
symptoms: Clunk, pop or knock from front end over bumps
Noise under acceleration or braking
Steering wander or looseness in severe cases

before.title: Front Upper Control Arm Ball Joint Squeak/Creak
before.description: A very common Model 3 (and Model Y) complaint is a squeaking or dry-hinge/creaking noise from the front suspension at low speed and over bumps, traced to the front upper control arm (FUCA) ball joint. Water bypasses the ball-joint seal, washing out the grease and allowing metal-on-metal corrosion. The noise is often reproducible by opening the frunk and pushing down on the front of the car. Tesla frequently replaces the arms under warranty and has covered labor as 'goodwill' even on some out-of-warranty cars.
before.solution: Replace the front upper control arm(s); Tesla's fix is the complete FUCA assembly (Tesla PN family 1044321-00-x). Aftermarket ball-joint-only kits (e.g., Unplugged Performance) or camber-adjustable arms exist. Confirm it is the FUCA and not a wheel bearing before replacing; some cars need both. A four-wheel alignment is recommended afterward.
symptoms: Squeak or dry-hinge creak from front end at low speed
Noise over bumps and when pushing down on the frunk
Creaking when turning or on uneven pavement

before.title: Frozen Door Handles in Cold Weather (Can't Enter Car)
before.description: In snow/ice, moisture inside the flush pivoting door handle freezes and the handle will not depress/deploy, locking owners out. Tesla's own owner's manual acknowledges ice buildup can prevent the handle from opening. Forcing a frozen handle can damage the internal mechanism, and handle replacement runs $300-600+.
before.solution: Tesla advises firm strikes around the handle perimeter ('like knocking on a door') to break the ice, then cycling the handle a few times — NOT prying with tools. Precondition/defrost the car from the app before departure, or open the driver door remotely via the app's Unlatch Door quick control. Preventively apply WD-40/silicone to the pivot pins. If the handle mechanism is damaged, replace the handle assembly.
symptoms: Door handle won't depress or pop out in freezing weather
Handle feels stuck/iced
Have to enter via another door or the app

before.title: Model 3 / Y Heat Pump EXV Stuck-Open Recall (22V-050)
before.description: NHTSA recall 22V-050 covered Model 3 (built Feb 13, 2021 - Jan 12, 2022), Model Y (built Jun 30, 2021 - Jan 11, 2022), Model S (built Mar 5, 2021 - Jan 12, 2022), and Model X (built Oct 31, 2021 - Jan 11, 2022) on firmware releases 2021.44 through 2021.44.30.6. The Electronic Expansion Valve (EXV) in the heat pump system could remain open after a comms loss with the heat pump, trapping refrigerant in the evaporator and triggering compressor self-shutdown — resulting in no cabin heat and no defrost. The octovalve coolant manifold is part of the affected thermal system.
before.solution: Recall remedy was OTA firmware update to 2021.44.30.7 or later, which reintroduces a software command to close the EXV. Confirm software is current. Hardware-level octovalve / heat pump replacement (out of warranty) $600-$1,500.
symptoms: no heat
no defrost
preconditioning fails
HV battery cold

before.title: Loss of Power Steering Assist — EPAS Circuit Board Recall
before.description: On certain 2023 Model 3/Y cars, the electronic power-assisted steering (EPAS) printed circuit board can become overstressed during low-speed maneuvering, causing loss of power steering assist when the car stops and accelerates again. Drivers must apply much greater steering effort, raising crash risk. Tesla recalled ~376,000-380,000 vehicles.
before.solution: Install software release 2023.38.4 or later, which prevents the EPAS overstress at 0 mph — delivered over-the-air, no service visit required. Verify the car is updated and check VIN against the recall. If assist is already lost/hardware-damaged, the EPAS rack/motor assembly is replaced (out-of-recall cost is far higher).
symptoms: Steering suddenly heavy after stopping then accelerating
'Power steering assist reduced' warning
Notably increased steering effort at low speed

before.title: Premature Inner-Edge Tire Wear (Camber/Toe Alignment)
before.description: Model 3 owners widely report tires wearing out on the inner edge well before expected mileage. Causes are factory negative camber (for handling), toe misalignment, high instant torque, and overinflation; only toe is adjustable from the factory (camber is fixed unless aftermarket arms are added). before.title: Rearview / Backup Camera Loss (Firmware Recall + Trunk-Lid Coax Wear)
before.description: The backup camera image can fail to display when shifting to reverse. Two documented root causes: (1) a firmware/I2C stability defect on certain 2023-2024 cars addressed by NHTSA recall 24V-035, and (2) mechanical wear of the coaxial camera cable routed through the trunk-lid harness, which frays after repeated trunk opening/closing and cuts the video feed. Loss of the reversing image is a safety/visibility concern.
before.solution: For the software cause, install the recall firmware (2023.44.30.7 or later) via OTA — no service visit needed; verify VIN against Tesla's and NHTSA's recall lookup. For the coax/harness wear, Tesla replaces the trunk-lid camera cable/harness. If the screen is otherwise fine and only the camera is black, suspect the harness first.
symptoms: Black or blank screen where the reverse camera should appear
Intermittent camera loss when opening/closing trunk
Camera works then drops out in cold temperatures

before.title: Taillight Condensation & Trunk-Lid Water Leak
before.description: Water pools inside the sheet-metal trunk lid and/or condensation forms inside the taillights due to unsealed seams and inadequate taillight gaskets. Owners report water sloshing in the trunk lid and moisture behind the lenses. Early build (2017-2019) cars are worst; sealing improved from 2018 on. Trapped water can eventually reach the taillight electronics.
before.solution: Minor taillight fogging can be cleared with gentle heat (hair dryer) so humid air escapes the vent. For persistent water intrusion, Tesla service reseals the trunk-lid seams / replaces the pinched or under-thick taillight gasket, generally under warranty. Some owners add butyl sealant to the taillight gasket as a DIY fix.
symptoms: Fog/condensation inside taillight lenses
Water sloshing sound in the trunk lid
Standing water in trunk well after rain or washing

before.title: Touchscreen Yellow Border / Yellow Band Around Display
before.description: A faint yellow-to-brown band appears around the perimeter of the center touchscreen, caused by degradation of an adhesive/optical layer in the display accelerated by heat and UV exposure. It is cosmetic (touch still works) but widely reported and was the subject of an extended owner backlash before Tesla developed a fix.
before.solution: Tesla's official remedy is a UV-light fixture applied to the screen for ~2-3 hours at a Service Center (cannot be done by Mobile Service); it is typically free under the basic warranty. The fix does NOT require replacing the MCU or screen. DIY owners have used a 365-370nm UV nail lamp with mixed results. If the border returns or the panel is otherwise failing, the display assembly is replaced.
symptoms: Yellow or brown band framing the touchscreen
Discoloration worst at the screen edges
More visible in bright/hot conditions

before.title: Vampire / Phantom Battery Drain While Parked
before.description: The high-voltage battery slowly loses charge while parked because background systems stay awake. Normal drain is under ~1%/day, but owners report much higher losses (several percent per day) when Sentry Mode, Cabin Overheat Protection, Summon Standby, Dog/Camp mode, or third-party apps repeatedly wake the car and prevent it from sleeping.
before.solution: Let the car sleep (7-10 min after driving/charging). Set a Home favorite so Sentry auto-disables there; turn off Sentry/Cabin Overheat Protection/Summon Standby when not needed; limit frequent-polling third-party apps; disable 'Keep Accessory Power On.' Persistent abnormal drain that doesn't sleep can indicate a component keeping the car awake — log a service ticket.
symptoms: Several percent range lost overnight while parked
Car won't 'sleep' in the app
Higher drain with Sentry Mode enabled

before.title: Windshield/Cabin Fogging with A/C + Recirculation in Cold
before.description: In cold, humid conditions the windshield and side glass can fog rapidly (sometimes within ~30 seconds) when recirculation is on, because humid cabin air is retained instead of exhausted. Some owners feel the heat-pump-equipped cars dehumidify less aggressively than the older resistive A/C setup. It is largely an HVAC-mode/behavior issue rather than a defect, but it is a frequent and safety-relevant complaint.
before.solution: Keep climate on Auto (which dehumidifies), turn recirculation OFF in cold weather so moist air is exhausted, and use the defog/defrost button (turns on A/C + max heat + fan) to clear glass quickly. Keep cabin filter fresh and remove wet floor mats/snow that add humidity. If fogging persists with fresh air selected, have the HVAC/heat-pump dehumidification checked.
symptoms: Windshield fogs quickly with A/C and recirculation on
Interior glass condensation in cold/damp weather
Fog returns unless defrost mode is used

before.title: Model 3 / Y 12V Auxiliary Battery Premature Failure
before.description: Pre-Highland Model 3 and pre-Juniper Model Y used a small lead-acid AGM 12V auxiliary battery that often fails in 12-24 months — well below typical 12V lifespan. Tesla switched to a lithium-ion 12V starting 2021-2022 (varies by build date) which lasts much longer but can also fail with "Power Off" warnings or refusing to wake. Symptoms: "12V Battery Needs Service" alert, car refusing to wake from sleep, sentry mode glitches.
before.solution: Lead-acid 12V replacement $150-$250 part + $100-$200 service-center install. Lithium 12V $200-$300 part. DIY is feasible but disabling HV system safely is critical. Many 2018-2020 Model 3 owners report needing 2-3 replacements before lithium retrofit.
symptoms: 12V needs service alert
will not wake
sentry mode failed
power off warning

before.title: Model 3 / Y Paint Thickness + Chipping
before.description: Tesla paint is notoriously thinner than industry standard — typically 100-120 microns vs 150-180 for German/Japanese makes. before.title: Model 3 / Y Phantom Braking on Autopilot
before.description: Model 3 and Y on Autopilot or TACC report unexpected hard braking events — "phantom braking" — most often at highway speed in response to non-existent obstacles, shadows, overpasses, or oncoming traffic in opposite lanes. NHTSA investigation PE22-002 opened in 2022 covering 416,000 vehicles after 354 complaints, including some rear-end collisions. Tesla's shift from radar to "Tesla Vision" (vision-only) intensified reports.
before.solution: Update to latest firmware (FSD beta or production); some specific software versions are notably worse. Configure following distance to max (7). Disable Autopilot on roads where phantom braking is frequent. NHTSA investigation remains active — Tesla has not issued a formal recall as of writing.
symptoms: sudden braking
autopilot brake event
TACC slowdown
rear-end risk
